questions.question: Explain the four long-term causes of World War I and show how the assassination at Sarajevo led to a general war within five weeks.
questions.expected_answer: Militarism: arms race and large armies made leaders ready to fight. Alliances: Triple Alliance and Triple Entente meant a local quarrel drew in all members. Imperialism: rivalry for colonies created tension. Nationalism: pride and Slav nationalism in the Balkans threatened Austria-Hungary. After Princip killed Franz Ferdinand on 28 June 1914, Austria-Hungary, backed by Germany, declared war on Serbia; Russia mobilised to support Serbia; Germany declared war on Russia and France and invaded Belgium; Britain declared war on Germany on 4 August.

questions.question: Describe South Africa's involvement in World War I, including the campaign in German South West Africa, Delville Wood and the SS Mendi.
questions.expected_answer: As a British dominion, South Africa was at war from August 1914. Its forces conquered German South West Africa in 1915 after putting down an Afrikaner rebellion that opposed fighting for Britain. At Delville Wood in July 1916 about 3 000 men of the South African Brigade held the wood for six days under heavy shelling; fewer than 800 answered the roll call. Black South Africans could not carry arms; about 25 000 served in the South African Native Labour Corps. On 21 February 1917 the SS Mendi sank after a collision off the Isle of Wight and more than 600 men died.

questions.question: Distinguish between primary and secondary sources and explain how you would judge the reliability of a recruiting poster from 1915.
questions.expected_answer: A primary source was produced at the time by someone involved; a secondary source was produced later by someone studying the past. For the poster ask who made it, when, why and for whom: it was made by the government to persuade men to enlist, so it is unreliable as a description of war but reliable and useful as evidence of propaganda and official attitudes. Cross-check with other sources.
